issue.title: sase/memory/build_and_run.md still claims the diff-scoped lane "takes no suite-gate lease"
issue.description:
Found by the sase-gj land agent. Caused by sase-gj.3 (the middle gear), which made the claim false and did not update the always-loaded memory.

Before sase-gj.3, `just check`'s scoped test lane was serial and took no suite-gate lease at all. The middle gear changed that: when RULE_SERIAL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED is the only reason a selection would escalate, tests/_test_selection_gear.engage_scoped_gear() builds a real `WorkerTokenLease` against `gate_directory()` and calls `try_acquire()`, then runs the selection at the granted width. The lease is bounded (ceiling 4) and strictly non-blocking — a refused grant escalates rather than queues — so the promise that actually matters to agents ("never waits behind another agent's run") still holds, but "takes no suite-gate lease" is now false whenever the gear engages.

STALE IN (both lines carry it):
  sase/memory/build_and_run.md:13  — `just check` comment block: "test lane that takes no suite-gate lease"
  sase/memory/build_and_run.md:27  — "...static import-graph closure and takes no suite-gate lease."

Those propagate verbatim into the generated provider shims AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, OPENCODE.md, and QWEN.md (lines 20 and 34 of each), so every agent in this repo currently reads the false claim in its always-loaded Tier 1 memory.

ALREADY FIXED, for reference on the wording to match:
  docs/development.md:60 — "The scoped run is serial (`-n 1`) unless the middle gear below wins it a small lease, and it never queues behind other agents' runs either way." (sase-gj.7)
  Justfile — the `test-scoped` and `check` recipe comments, corrected by the sase-gj land agent.

Scope: correct both lines in sase/memory/build_and_run.md, then run `sase memory init` to regenerate AGENTS.md and the provider shims. NOTE FOR THE ASSIGNEE: editing sase/memory/*.md requires the user's explicit permission in the conversation that does the work — per CLAUDE.md, authorization recorded in a bead description does not count. The land agent left this as a task for exactly that reason rather than editing memory without permission. Once the user asks for the edit, running `sase memory init` afterwards is mandatory and needs no separate approval.
